title: My digital life
paragraphs: My name is Amir Bekzhanov and I am a Computer Science student at WKU. People always say that students of my generation spend too much time on technology — and honestly, I think they are right! But in my case, technology is not just entertainment: it is the central tool of my education, my social life, and my daily routine. In this essay, I want to describe my digital life honestly — the good parts and the not-so-good parts.

I always start my day by checking my phone. The alarm rings at 7:00 am, and before I even get out of bed, I check my messages, scroll through my news feed for about five minutes, and look at the weather app to decide what to wear. I know this is a bad habit — experts say you should never look at screens in the first thirty minutes of the day — but I find it very difficult to resist. I usually have about forty-seven unread messages by morning, mostly in group chats.

During the day, I use my laptop constantly for my studies. I take notes in Google Docs during every lecture so that I can access them from any device. I often use YouTube to watch tutorial videos when I do not understand something from the lecture. My favourite channels are about programming, mathematics, and artificial intelligence. I sometimes spend two or three hours watching educational videos in the evening — which my roommate says is "watching TV with extra steps".

For communication, I use WhatsApp for family and close friends, Telegram for university group chats, and Instagram for staying connected with a wider social circle. I rarely use phone calls anymore — I prefer texting because it is faster and less interrupting. The only person I always call is my grandmother, who still does not trust messaging apps and insists on a proper phone conversation every Sunday evening.

In terms of studying, technology has completely transformed how I learn. I use Anki — a spaced repetition app — to memorise English vocabulary. I use Notion to organise my notes, deadlines, and project plans. I often use ChatGPT to check my English writing or to explain a complex programming concept in simple terms. My professor has mixed feelings about this, but I always tell him: "A good programmer uses every tool available."

However, I also recognise the negative sides of my digital habits. I sometimes waste a lot of time on social media without realising it. I will open Instagram to check one notification and, forty minutes later, I am still scrolling through videos of cats and cooking recipes. I never set a screen time limit, which is a mistake I plan to fix soon. Sleep is another problem: I often use my phone in bed, which makes it harder to fall asleep quickly.

I need to learn to use technology more intentionally. I want to set a specific "no screen" time in the evening — perhaps from 10 pm to bedtime. I plan to turn off all notifications except from family during lecture hours. I also hope to spend more time reading physical books, because I notice that long reading sessions on screens give me headaches in a way that paper books never do.

Technology is neither good nor bad in itself — it depends entirely on how you use it. As a Computer Science student, I believe it is my responsibility to be a smart and intentional digital citizen. I want to be the person who controls technology, not the person who technology controls. Starting tomorrow — or, realistically, starting next Monday! 😄

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Amir, you're always on your phone. Do you ever put it down?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Ha! I check it about sixty times a day. It's terrible. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I try to keep it off during dance practice — three hours without a phone feels amazing!

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Three hours? I can barely manage three minutes. Which apps do you use most?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Instagram for dancing content, and Telegram for the university groups. What about you?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Same, plus YouTube for programming tutorials. I sometimes watch for three hours straight.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: That's a lot! Do you use any apps for studying — not just entertainment?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Yes! Anki for vocabulary, Notion for organisation, Google Docs for notes. I rarely use paper anymore.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I need to try Anki — my English vocabulary is terrible. How often do you use it?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I try to do fifteen minutes every morning. I usually manage it except on Monday after football.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: What's your biggest bad habit with tech?

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: Using my phone in bed. I never fall asleep before midnight because of it. You?

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Checking Instagram first thing in the morning. I always regret it immediately!

grammarNote:
Наречия частотности (frequency adverbs) отвечают на вопрос "КАК ЧАСТО?" и всегда используются вместе с Present Simple. Они показывают, насколько регулярно что-то происходит.

Шкала частотности от 100% до 0%:
always (100%) → usually (80%) → often (60%) → sometimes (40%) → rarely/seldom (20%) → never (0%)

📍 МЕСТО В ПРЕДЛОЖЕНИИ — главное правило:

① С обычными глаголами → ПЕРЕД глаголом:
   "I always check my phone." · "She usually studies in the library."
   "He often watches tutorials." · "They sometimes forget their password."

② С глаголом "to be" → ПОСЛЕ глагола "be":
   "I am always on time." (НЕ "I always am on time.")
   "She is never late." · "They are usually tired after class."
   "He is sometimes stressed about exams."

③ В вопросах и коротких ответах:
   "How often do you check social media?" — "I check it constantly!"
   "Do you always eat breakfast?" — "I usually do, but sometimes I skip it."

⚠️ ТИПИЧНЫЕ ОШИБКИ:
❌ "I check always my phone." → ✅ "I always check my phone."
❌ "She usually is late." → ✅ "She is usually late." (после be!)
❌ "Sometimes I am go." → ✅ "Sometimes I go." (never is + go!)
